video_metadata.working_title: TEXAS 1995 Cold Case Solved After 26 Years — Justice for Mary Catherine Edwards
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: In January 1995 Beaumont schoolteacher Mary Catherine Edwards, 31, was found handcuffed and dead in the bathtub of her townhome; 26 years later Othram's forensic genetic genealogy and a trash pull in Ohio identified Clayton Bernard Foreman, a man from her high school whose 1982 wedding she had been a bridesmaid in, and a Jefferson County jury convicted him of capital murder in March 2024.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into quiet outrage at how close and familiar the killer was, then relief through science and persistent detectives

protagonist._instructions: Victim-centred story. The convicted man is described in supporting_characters.
protagonist.full_name: Mary Catherine Edwards (often called Catherine in reporting)
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Elementary school teacher at Price Elementary School, Beaumont (12NewsNow URL slug describes her as a 5th-grade teacher; single-sourced)
protagonist.location: Her townhome (townhouse) in Beaumont, Jefferson County, Texas
protagonist.physical_description: Not used; real photos only. She had an identical twin sister, Allison.
protagonist.background_brief: Beaumont native; identical twin of Allison Edwards Brocato; attended the same high school as Clayton Foreman (Forest Park High School per Foreman's 1978 graduation and reports that they were schoolmates); she and her twin were good friends with Dianna Coe and served as bridesmaids at Coe's 1982 wedding to Foreman; became a teacher and, per her twin's trial testimony, loved her students dearly and called them all her kids.
protagonist.psychological_profile: Not documented beyond family testimony; do not speculate.
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: She called all of her students 'her kids' (Allison Brocato's trial testimony, as reported).

individuals.name: Mary Catherine Edwards
individuals.role_or_profession: Elementary school teacher, Price Elementary, Beaumont
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Sexually assaulted and killed in her townhome; found handcuffed in the bathtub on January 14, 1995; autopsy: drowning and asphyxiation (later described by Det. Lewallen as suffocation by compression because there was not enough fluid in her lungs).
individuals.humanizing_detail: Called her students 'her kids'; identical twin.

individuals.name: Allison Edwards Brocato
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Twin; also a bridesmaid at the 1982 Foreman–Coe wedding
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Went with her mother to the townhome on January 14, 1995 and is heard on the 911 call ('My sister's dead'); testified at trial in 2024 about how close the twins were.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Testified through tears about the day her sister died.
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: 'My sister's dead.' (911 call transcript excerpt, KFDM)

individuals.name: Edwards' parents (names not confirmed in sources)
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: CBS reports her parents found her; KFDM reports her mother and sister described finding her on the 911 call.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Could not reach her and went to check on her.
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: KFDM headline quotes the 911 call: 'My daughter's been murdered' (speaker not confirmed in excerpt).

individuals.name: Woman assaulted in 1981 (name withheld)
individuals.role_or_profession: 19 years old in 1981; described as a former high school classmate of Foreman
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Testified in 2024 that Foreman bound her hands behind her back with a belt and assaulted her at knifepoint in his car before driving her home; Foreman pleaded guilty to aggravated assault and received 3 years deferred adjudication.

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: Edwards' family, her students and colleagues at Price Elementary, Beaumont community
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: 29 years from the murder to the verdict

characters.name: Clayton Bernard Foreman
characters.key_actions_they_took: 1978 graduate of Forest Park High School, Beaumont; in 1981 pleaded guilty to aggravated assault in an attack on a 19-year-old woman (3 years deferred adjudication); married Dianna Coe in 1982 with Mary Catherine and Allison Edwards as bridesmaids; not a person of interest in the original investigation; by 2021 living in Reynoldsburg, Franklin County, Ohio, reportedly working as a rideshare driver; arrested April 2021 at age 61; told investigators the twins had been bridesmaids at his wedding but that he had no interactions with them beyond it; convicted at 63; life sentence.
characters.notable_quotes: Per Dianna Coe (CBS 48 Hours), when she called him crying that somebody had murdered Catherine, he answered 'Oh, really?' with no emotion.

characters.name: Dianna Coe
characters.role_in_story: Foreman's first wife; friend of the Edwards twins; same high school
characters.key_actions_they_took: Told 48 Hours / testified that Foreman kept a billy club by the bed 'for protection' and had ordered handcuffs that hung over the rearview mirror; recalled his flat reaction to the news of the murder.

characters.name: Det. Aaron Lewallen
characters.role_in_story: Beaumont Police Department detective who worked the cold case
characters.key_actions_they_took: Received the genealogy lead; built the case; co-conducted the recorded interview with Foreman; spoke to 48 Hours.
characters.notable_quotes: Paraphrased (CBS): originally they believed she might have been drowned, but there was not enough fluid in her lungs; it became suffocation by compression.

characters.name: Texas Ranger Brandon Bess
characters.role_in_story: Texas Rangers Unsolved Crimes Investigation Program
characters.key_actions_they_took: Co-conducted the 50-minute recorded interview with Foreman.
characters.notable_quotes: Single-sourced fragment 'There's no justice' (context: loss of life) — not used in script.

characters.name: Shera LaPoint
characters.key_actions_they_took: Helped build the family trees (ISHI Report).

characters.name: Othram Inc. (The Woodlands, Texas; CEO David Mittelman)
characters.key_actions_they_took: Received the crime-scene DNA in April 2020; built a profile of more than half a million markers for genetic genealogy.

characters.name: Bob Wortham
characters.key_actions_they_took: Said that on his first day in office he called Chief Singletary and asked him to put people on the Edwards case; credited Beaumont PD.

characters.name: Judge John Stevens
characters.role_in_story: Criminal District Court of Jefferson County
characters.key_actions_they_took: Presided over the trial; allowed the interview video; imposed life sentence.

characters.name: Tom Burbank
characters.key_actions_they_took: Argued the interview violated Foreman's rights and was conducted under false pretenses; no defense witnesses were called.

characters.name: Natalie Morales
characters.key_actions_they_took: Reported 'Tracking the Killer of Mary Catherine Edwards' (Nov 2024; re-aired Jan 2026).

Clayton Foreman graduates.
events.significance: Shared school with Edwards, Coe and the 1981 victim.

events.what_happened: Foreman binds a 19-year-old woman's hands behind her back with a belt and assaults her at knifepoint in his car; pleads guilty to aggravated assault; 3 years deferred adjudication.
events.significance: Admitted at trial; appeals court found 12 similarities with the Edwards murder.

events.what_happened: Foreman marries Dianna Coe; Mary Catherine and Allison Edwards are bridesmaids.
events.significance: The personal link no one connected for 26 years.

events.what_happened: Edwards last seen; prosecutors and police date the rape and murder to this day.
Family cannot reach her; mother and twin (CBS: parents) find her in the upstairs bathroom, handcuffed behind her back, head in the water of the bathtub; 911 call.
Autopsy: drowning and asphyxiation; sexual assault confirmed; semen collected; police-grade Smith & Wesson handcuffs, a T-shirt and the sexual assault kit preserved.
events.significance: The DNA that would solve the case 26 years later.

events.what_happened: Beaumont PD and Texas Rangers investigate; handcuff serial numbers traced without result; law enforcement officers questioned without result.
events.significance: Fear the killer was a police officer; Foreman never a person of interest.

events.what_happened: STR profile from unknown male searched in CODIS: no match.
Bob Wortham takes office as DA; on his first day calls Chief Singletary to put people on the case.
Texas Rangers and Beaumont PD renew efforts and offer a $6,000 reward.
Crime-scene DNA sent to Othram; profile of more than half a million markers built for forensic genetic genealogy.
Closest match: a woman in Louisiana, apparently a second cousin; lead passed to Det. Aaron Lewallen; trees built with genealogist Shera LaPoint; trees point to Clayton Foreman.

events.date: Early 2021 (exact date not public in sources)
events.what_happened: Investigators collect discarded items from Foreman's curb; affidavit: trash DNA matches the semen from 1995.
Foreman, 61, arrested; Jefferson County Sheriff's aviation unit flew investigators; recorded 50-minute interview with Ranger Brandon Bess and Det. Aaron Lewallen.
events.significance: 26 years and about 3 months after the murder (9,599 days to April 26).

events.what_happened: Foreman appears to contest extradition; Ohio judge orders him returned by July 6; transported to Jefferson County Jail on June 15, 2021 (single-sourced).

events.what_happened: Jury selection begins before Judge John Stevens; testimony begins March 12 with the 911 call.
Testimony: 911 call, twin sister, handcuffs/T-shirt/kit, DNA experts, Dianna Coe, 1981 victim; interview video admitted over defense objection; no defense witnesses.
Jury finds Foreman, 63, guilty of capital murder after about 50 minutes (another report: 52); automatic life sentence; parole eligibility reported as 2061 (Texas Monthly: 30 years).

the_moment.what_is_happening: Her family cannot reach her, goes to her townhome, and finds her in the upstairs bathroom.
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: Police-grade handcuffs; no forced entry; she seemed to know her killer.
the_moment.ironic_twist: The man whose DNA was left behind had stood at an altar in 1982 while she and her twin stood beside his bride as bridesmaids.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who did Mary Catherine Edwards let into her home, and why did it take 26 years and a cousin in Louisiana to find out?

the_method.technique_name: Forensic genetic genealogy (FGG) with Othram's genome sequencing
step_by_step_explanation: 1995: semen preserved in the sexual assault kit.
STR profile (about 20 markers) searched in CODIS: no match.
April 2020: sample to Othram, which built a profile of more than half a million markers (SNPs).
Profile compared with consenting users in genealogy databases.
Closest match: a woman in Louisiana, about a second cousin (shares great-grandparents).
Genealogists build family trees forward from shared ancestors using public records; tree narrows to Clayton Foreman.
Discarded items from Foreman's curb in Reynoldsburg, Ohio tested: match to 1995 semen.
Arrest; confirmation testing; trial DNA testimony.
the_method.why_it_worked: The DNA had been preserved; Foreman's 1981 offense was resolved by a plea before DNA databases existed, so he was never in CODIS; consumer genealogy databases contained a distant relative.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The FBI's national DNA index (launched nationally in October 1998) compares about 20 short repeated markers; it only finds people already in it.
Hundreds of thousands of single-letter spelling points in the genome; enough to detect distant cousins.
Someone who shares a set of great-grandparents with you.
Police may collect items a person has put out for garbage collection and test them.
A Texas form of probation after a guilty plea; if completed, no final conviction is entered.
Evidence of an earlier act admitted not to show bad character but for identity, intent or motive.

the_method.scale_of_operation: Half a million markers; one Louisiana second cousin; one trash pull.

systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: The pre-DNA-database criminal justice system of the early 1980s and the 1995 investigation's limits
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Identify offenders with prior violent sexual offenses.
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: The 1981 attack was resolved by a plea to aggravated assault with deferred adjudication, long before Texas DNA collection; Foreman was not a person of interest in 1995; investigators focused on the police-grade handcuffs.
specific_incompetence_examples: Handcuff serial numbers traced with no result
Law enforcement officers questioned with no result
26 years and 3 months to an arrest
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The killer was in the victim's own social circle, on her own high school's alumni list and in her bridesmaid photos; the 1981 victim's hands had also been bound behind her back.

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Beaumont Police Department; Texas Rangers Unsolved Crimes Investigation Program; Othram; Jefferson County Criminal District Attorney's Office
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Fear that the killer was a law enforcement officer because of the police-grade handcuffs.
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Othram genealogy profile → Louisiana second cousin → family tree → Clayton Foreman.
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Discarded trash at his Reynoldsburg home carried his DNA.

the_confrontation.scene_description: Investigators flown in by the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office aviation unit; Foreman taken into custody; recorded 50-minute interview with Ranger Bess and Det. Lewallen.
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: Told investigators the twins were bridesmaids at his 1982 wedding but that he had no interactions with them beyond it.
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: The interview began as a 'conversation'; defense later called it false pretenses; judge admitted it.

legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: 911 call; twin sister Allison Brocato; Dianna Coe (billy club, handcuffs, 'Oh, really?'); 1981 victim; DNA experts; handcuffs, T-shirt and sexual assault kit shown to jury.

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: ...been a long, emotional journey to finally see justice and closure.

legal_resolution.sentence_received: Automatic life in TDCJ (death penalty not sought at trial); parole eligibility reported as 2061 (Texas Monthly says 30 years; 40-year rule for capital life for 1993–2005 offenses supports 2061).
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: Did not testify; no defense witnesses.
legal_resolution.current_status: As of October 2026: serving life in TDCJ; conviction affirmed by the Ninth Court of Appeals (Beaumont), reported early January 2026. No report found of a petition for discretionary review outcome.

key_locations.physical_description: Two-storey townhome with an upstairs bathroom (exact address not used)

Jefferson County seat on the Neches River in Southeast Texas; part of the Golden Triangle with Port Arthur and Orange; Spindletop oil gusher of January 10, 1901; Lamar University; about 114,000 residents in 1990
Suburb east of Columbus, Franklin County

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: The most dangerous person may be someone familiar enough to be let in the door.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: No forced entry; a known face.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Old violent offenses that predate DNA databases can hide offenders for decades; preserved evidence and genealogy can still find them.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: Forensic genetic genealogy funding and Othram's case work continue in 2026.
